bifrost: none for Matter or Thread; nearby: springboard/src/net/wifi.rs and springboard/src/net/wifi_config.rs (Wi-Fi credentials), springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs (BlueZ mgmt pairing), springboard/src/net/share.rs (LAN beacon)
summary: Apple's Matter framework is a controller API for Matter smart-home accessories: commissioning, cluster reads and writes, and subscriptions. BifrOSt now decodes Matter setup codes (the QR payload and the manual pairing code) and parses commissionable and operational DNS-SD names and TXT records, all in springboard/core/src/matter.rs. It still has no controller, fabric or certificate store, no Thread, no cluster client and no SDK API, so the framework stays partial.

features.feature: Onboarding a Matter device (setup code, QR payload parsing)
features.note: Setup payload decoding is in core: the QR code (MT: and Base38, 88-bit payload) and the 11 and 21 digit manual pairing code with its Verhoeff check digit. Nothing feeds it from a camera or a BLE scan yet, so the onboarding flow does not start.
No fabric or operational certificate issuer. Link keys are stored in bluetooth.ini (springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs), which is not a Matter credential store.
Wi-Fi join and saved network configuration exist. There is no Thread network, no Thread border router and no device attestation.

features.feature: Accessory control (attribute read/write, command invoke, subscriptions)
features.apple: MTRDevice, MTRReadParams, MTRWriteParams, MTRSubscribeParams, MTRAttributePath, MTRCommandPath
features.note: Wave 6 (b05, main): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on Midget. No client for the Matter interaction model and no SDK API for accessories.

features.feature: Clusters (typed On/Off, Level Control, Switch and others)
features.apple: MTRBaseClusterLevelControl, MTRBaseClusterApplicationLauncher and about 200 more cluster classes
features.note: No cluster model of any kind. The control centre toggles in springboard/src/shell/control_center.rs are local system settings, not accessories.

features.feature: Local network discovery of accessories (DNS-SD and mDNS)
features.apple: Commissioned accessories are found over the local network by the controller (framework-internal)
features.bifrost: springboard/core/src/matter.rs (service_kind, commissionable_from_txt, operational_from_instance); the transport is still springboard/src/net/share.rs
features.note: Parses the _matterc._udp and _matter._tcp instance names and the commissionable TXT keys (D, VP, CM, DN, PH). There is no mDNS responder or querier, and apps cannot browse services.

gaps: No Matter controller: no fabric, certificates, commissioning or interaction model, in the shell or the SDK.
No Thread support: no border router, no Thread network credentials and no OpenThread stack.

No mDNS or DNS-SD transport: the name and TXT parsers in springboard/core/src/matter.rs have no multicast responder or querier, and apps cannot browse services. The only LAN beacon is springboard/src/net/share.rs.
No BLE commissioning path, and no camera or scan source for setup codes. The Bluetooth module handles classic pairing only (springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs).
No SDK API or app-facing surface for smart-home accessories, and no Home-style app. Whether BifrOSt should add one is a product decision, not a technical gap.
